note: Hand-labelled sample for the validity pass. `contradictions` lists the assignment classes that are genuinely inconsistent, by the names the code writes; `tri` is the verdict a correct pass should reach for the case: false when some class is contradictory, true when the code is consistent and says at least one definite type, unknown when nothing definite is stated. The pass is deliberately stricter than pyright's inference: pyright accepts `x = 1` then `x = "one"` because it re-narrows an unannotated name, while this sample treats two unrelated definite types reaching one location as the defect the pass exists to report. `x = None` then `x = 1` is the Optional idiom and is clean. Two cases are expected to be missed without pyright (c14, and c11/c22 where only a class attribute declares a type), and each says so.
